Saturday. Vikas lived on the low side of the river town and had watched water reach the gate twice. Parveen, a neighbour, came over to help pack a bag: photocopied papers in a plastic pouch, the family's tablets as listed by the doctor, some cash, a torch and a charger. They put it by the door.
Wednesday night. The siren sounded at eleven. Vikas lifted the bag, called out to the family, locked the door and led everyone up the lane to the high school within minutes. Nobody had to search for anything.
The next Sunday. Back home, Vikas checked the bag, swapped the torch's batteries and added a spare pair of socks.

qa.q: What did Vikas do with the bag when the siren sounded?
qa.a: Vikas lifted the bag, called out to the family and led everyone up the lane to the high school.

qa.q: What was Vikas probably feeling when the siren went at eleven?
qa.a: Vikas was alarmed but steady, since the bag was ready and no decisions had to be made under stress.

qa.q: What could Vikas do to keep the bag ready for next time?
qa.a: Vikas could check the bag on a regular date, replace the batteries and refresh the papers and tablets.

qa.q: How might Parveen have felt seeing the family leave so fast?
qa.a: Parveen was probably relieved and reassured that the packing had helped, since nobody had to search for anything.

grounding: The passage shows a person in a flood-prone area who keeps a ready bag with papers, medicines, cash, torch and charger so that leaving takes minutes.

subtype: Approach: preparing a go-bag in advance [Action]
passage: Alka, you keep asking why your Himani Ma'am keeps a red bag behind the office door. Sit, I'll tell you. Twelve years ago I was twenty-five, renting a room near the river in Silchar with my younger sister. In the first flood that year, we spent forty minutes in the dark hunting for her college certificates and her inhaler while the water climbed the stairs. After that, I packed one bag and kept it by the door: photocopies of our documents in a zip pouch, a strip of each medicine, two thousand in small notes, a torch, spare batteries, a charger and a power bank I topped up every Sunday. The next flood came in July. I woke my sister, lifted the bag, locked the door. Six minutes, Alka. We didn't have to decide anything.

qa.q: What did Himani keep in the zip pouch?
What had Himani felt during the search in the dark in the first flood?
qa.a: She had felt panicked and helpless, hunting for forty minutes for certificates and the inhaler while the water climbed the stairs.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Himani's story, and why did it work?
qa.a: Packing one bag after the first flood was the turning point, because in July leaving took six minutes with nothing left to decide.

qa.q: How might Himani's sister have experienced the July flood differently?
qa.a: Instead of a frantic search in the dark, she was woken and out in minutes, which was probably far less frightening.

grounding: It shows a young woman in a flood-prone area keeping a packed bag of document copies, medicines, cash, torch and charger so leaving takes minutes.

The rain had not stopped for two days, and Arohi's brother, Abhinav, was stuck in Cuttack with the buses cancelled. At 10.15 p.m. the panchayat's loudspeaker van crawled down the lane: water rising at the embankment, move to the school building.
Arohi didn't open a single cupboard. She took the green backpack from the hook by the door, the one she repacked every monsoon: copies of Baba's pension papers and their IDs in a plastic sleeve, his heart tablets, three thousand in small notes, a torch, the charger, the power bank. She put Baba's raincoat on him, locked the door and was at the school by 10.40.
From the school verandah she called Abhinav. 'We're out. We have everything. Don't try to come tonight.'

qa.q: Where did the loudspeaker van tell people to move?
How do you think Arohi felt when she called Abhinav from the verandah?
qa.a: She probably felt relieved and in control, able to reassure her brother that she and Baba were safe with everything they needed.

qa.q: What else could Arohi add to her plan, given that Abhinav was stuck away?
qa.a: She could agree a meeting place and a neighbour to contact with Abhinav in advance, so each knows what the other will do when roads close.

qa.q: How might Abhinav have been affected by the call?
qa.a: Stuck in Cuttack, Abhinav was spared a risky night journey and a long worry, because Arohi and Baba were already safe.

grounding: It shows a young woman in a flood-prone area whose ready bag of documents, medicines, cash, torch and charger lets her leave in minutes on a stormy night.
